# Every account gets inventory, and every account gets it free

URL: https://alphaflux.net/inventory
Section: Modules

Stock is never in one place. It is in trucks, in storage units, in a rented bay, in mobile units scattered across three states, and in the depot none of it was written down in. AlphaFlux knows all of it, and who is holding it.

## Inventory is included on the free plan, permanently

Most platforms treat stock as an enterprise feature. A one person operation with a van full of parts needs it just as much as a depot does, so it is not gated.

Every account gets items, movements, locations and low stock alerts at no cost, whether there is one technician or two hundred. What grows with the plan is scale, not capability: how many locations you can define, how much movement history you keep, and how far the reporting reaches.

The point is that the record starts on day one. A company that tracks its stock from the first van never has to reconstruct a year of purchases later, and never has to run an inventory count to find out what it owns.

- Items and stock levels: Parts, products and consumables with SKU, quantity on hand, reorder point, unit and cost.
- Locations that match reality: Trucks, vans, storage units, rented bays, depots, yards and branches, each with its own stock position.
- Movements, not just a number: Every change is a movement with a reason, a person and a time, so the quantity is explained rather than asserted.
- Low stock before it bites: Minimums per item and per location, with alerts when a truck is running out rather than when the next job fails.

## Chemical and controlled stock, signed in and out

Some things in a van are not ordinary stock. They are regulated, they have a usage rate, they must be accounted for, and an inspector may ask.

AlphaFlux tracks them the way they are actually used. A container is signed in when it is received, assigned to a technician or a location, and signed out when it is used or returned. The record shows who had it, when they took it, where it went and what remains.

That record is what turns a difficult conversation into a report. Usage per technician, usage per service, what was applied at a customer's property, and what is currently unaccounted for are all available as views rather than as an afternoon with a clipboard.

The same mechanism handles any stock that needs a chain of custody: calibrated instruments, keys, PPE, high value tools, controlled parts, and anything else where knowing that it left the building is not enough.

- Sign in, sign out: A container is received, assigned and consumed with a record at every step.
- Usage on the job: What was applied is recorded against the job, which is what most customer questions and inspections actually ask for.
- Safety data to hand: Regulatory detail, handling and dilution information available to the technician at the point of use rather than in a folder in the office.
- Anywhere it should not be: A reconciliation view that surfaces stock that has moved without a matching reason.

## Built for operations that do not fit one building

The same records serve a sole trader with a van and an operation with units in every time zone. These are the arrangements the module is designed around.

- Technician and vehicle stock: Every truck holds its own position, so the question where is that part is answered by naming the part rather than by ringing three technicians. A technician's stock moves when the job consumes it, not when someone remembers to update a sheet.
- Storage units and rented bays: A rented storage locker is a location like any other. It can hold stock, it can be transferred to and from, and it can be counted without an afternoon of driving to it and writing things down.
- Mobile and self contained units: Self contained units that move between sites, whether that is a mobile workshop, a solar powered field unit, a trailer or a container, are tracked as both an asset and a location. The unit has a position, a custodian and its own contents, and both move together.
- Branches, depots and yards: Branches hold bulk stock and issue it out. A transfer from a branch to a truck is one operation with a record at both ends, so both locations agree on what happened.
- Many companies, one view: An operator running several companies or several legal entities can hold each one's stock separately and still see a single consolidated position, because inventory is scoped to a company like every other record.
- Assets as well as consumables: Anything with a serial number, a warranty or a service interval can be tracked as an asset: who has it, where it is, when it was last serviced and when it is due. That covers instruments, machines, test equipment and vehicles.

## Day to day, it stays simple

A stock system only works if a technician will actually use it from a driveway. Everything here is designed to take seconds.

- Adjust in two taps: Search or scan, enter the quantity, pick a reason. Add a note if it needs one.
- Scan instead of type: Barcodes and QR codes read from the phone camera, which is what turns a stock take from a weekend into an hour.
- Consumed by the job: Parts used on a job are drawn down automatically when the job closes, and appear on the invoice from the same entry.
- Transfer between places: Move stock from depot to truck to site, with a record at each end and an in transit state so nothing is ever in two places.
- Counts that reconcile: Run a count on one location, see the variance against the system, and post the adjustment with a reason.
- Import and export: Bring a supplier price list or an existing spreadsheet in, and take the whole register out in a structured format whenever you want.

Nobody ever lost money knowing exactly what was in the truck and who took it out.

| Items | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Locations | 2 | 10 | 50 | Unlimited |

### Is inventory really free?

Yes, on every plan including the free one. Items, movements, sign in and sign out, scanning and low stock alerts are all included. What a plan changes is how many locations you can define and how long you keep movement history.

### How do I track chemicals across several technicians?

Each container is signed in when it is received and assigned to a technician or a location. When it is used, the amount consumed is recorded against the job, which leaves a per technician usage record and a per property application record. A reconciliation view shows anything that moved without a matching reason.

### Can I track stock that lives on a vehicle that moves between sites?

Yes. A mobile unit is treated as both an asset and a location, so it has a position, a custodian and its own contents, and all three move together. That covers mobile workshops, trailers, containers and remote units.

### I run more than one company. Can I see all their stock together?

Yes. Stock is scoped to a company, and an operator with access to several can see a consolidated position across all of them while each company's records stay separate.

### Does it handle stock in a truck being consumed by a job?

Yes. When a job is closed, the parts and consumables used are drawn from the technician's stock and carried onto the invoice. The technician does not enter the same information twice.

# Money that reconciles to the work, not to a memory

URL: https://alphaflux.net/billing
Section: Modules

The invoice is raised from the job that was actually completed, by the technician who completed it, with the parts that were actually used. Nothing is re-typed, so nothing drifts.

## The money side, end to end

From an agreed price at booking to a payment against the account, with a record at every step.

- Invoices from the work: Line items, labour, parts and taxes carried from the completed job, so the invoice describes what happened.
- Payments against an account: Applied to a customer, optionally tied to a job or an agreement, recorded in whole cents with the method and the date.
- Voided, never deleted: A payment entered in error is voided with a reason and a name. The row stays, and the voided total is reported separately from the posted total.
- Recurring billing: An agreement carries a price and a frequency, and the recurring revenue it produces is derived from the actual charges.
- Usage billing: For anything metered, a period's usage is read, the agreed margin applied, and an invoice issued per period with the underlying lines attached.
- Overdue, visible: Who owes what, how old the debt is, and what it is made of, so chasing is a list rather than a guess.

## A payment that can vanish is a payment nobody can audit

The most common way a small service business loses money is not theft. It is a payment that was deleted, a rate that was edited and nobody remembers why.

AlphaFlux does not delete financial records. A payment made in error is voided, which marks it as reversed, records who reversed it and why, and leaves the original row in place. The posted total excludes voided entries and the voided total is reported separately, so both numbers are always visible.

Rates, prices and commission percentages are recorded as they were when a transaction happened. Changing a rate in the future does not silently rewrite what someone was owed in the past, because the historical figure is stored rather than recomputed.

That discipline is what makes the numbers usable for a loan application, a tax return or a partner dispute. A figure you cannot trace back to the records that produced it is not a figure you can defend.

- Both totals, always: Posted and voided are reported side by side rather than netted into one misleading number.
- Historical values stay put: A price or a rate change applies forward. What happened last month is not recalculated.
- Rollups that match the detail: Totals by method, by day and by period always reconcile to the underlying rows.
- Every adjustment explained: An adjustment without a reason is not accepted, because the reason is the only part that cannot be reconstructed later.

## How the money is kept straight

These are the decisions that make the numbers hold up when someone else looks at them.

- Whole cents and basis points: All amounts are stored as whole cents and all rates as integer basis points. There is no floating point arithmetic anywhere near an invoice, which is why totals do not develop a mysterious fraction over a year.
- Recurring revenue from real charges: Monthly recurring revenue is calculated from the recurring charges that actually exist on agreements, split by frequency. It is not a projection and it is not a spreadsheet formula that assumes a renewal.
- Overdue is measured, not labelled: An account is overdue because of an unpaid balance with an age, not because a status field was set. The age is computed from the balance and its date, so it cannot go stale.
- Tax and totals as line items: Tax rates, discounts and surcharges are line items rather than adjustments applied at the end, so the arithmetic on an invoice can be followed from the first line to the total.
- Reports that match the ledger: The revenue figure on the dashboard and the total in the payment list come from the same records, so the executive view and the detail view cannot disagree.

## The invoice should be a by-product, not a task

In most service businesses, invoicing is a second job. The technician finishes the work on paper, someone types it up, parts get estimated from memory, and the invoice goes out a week later with the wrong total on it more often than anyone would like to admit.

When the job closes with its parts, its labour, its photos and its signature already attached, the invoice is largely already written. The office reviews it rather than reconstructing it. That is the entire argument for running the field and the money in one system.

It also changes what a customer experiences. The invoice arrives while the work is still fresh, with a photograph of what was done and the parts that were used, which is a considerably better conversation than a delayed total nobody can explain.


## Billing by plan


| Invoices | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Payments and voids | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Recurring agreements | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Overdue reporting | Basic | yes | yes | yes |
| Invoice from a completed job | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Usage billing and margins | no | no | yes | yes |
| Commission and split payouts | no | no | yes | yes |
| Consolidated reporting across locations | no | no | no | yes |

### Can I take card payments?

Payments are recorded against accounts and reconcile to the ledger. Card processing is connected through a payment provider, and the platform keeps the record of what was charged, what was collected and what was reversed, so the money is auditable whether it arrived by card, transfer, cheque or cash.

### What happens if I invoice the wrong amount?

You issue a corrected document. The original is not deleted, and the correction references it, which is how the paper trail stays intact for accounting and for the customer.

### Does it handle different pricing per district?

Yes, prices are per company and per service, and districts can carry different rate cards, which matters for companies operating in markets with different cost structures.

### Can I bill in something other than dollars?

Currency is a per company setting. Amounts are held as whole units in the company's currency, and the reporting is presented in the same currency the business operates in.

### How does the platform know what recurring revenue I have?

From the agreements themselves. Each agreement has a frequency and a price, and the monthly figure is calculated from those actual charges. If an agreement is cancelled, the number moves because the agreement did, not because someone updated a projection.

# Email marketing that sends from your own domain, not someone else's

URL: https://alphaflux.net/email-marketing
Section: Modules

Campaigns, sequences and follow ups that reach customers with your name on them, from your own domain, with the authentication records set up for you and every reply landing on the account.

## What the module covers

A campaign is a message sent on purpose to a list that consented. A sequence is a set of messages sent because something happened. Both belong to the customer record.

- Campaigns: Build a message, choose an audience, schedule it and read the result, with the content saved as a reusable template.
- Sequences and automations: Welcome a new customer, remind before a visit, follow up after a job, win back a lapsed account. Triggered by real events, not by a manual list.
- A visual builder: Drag blocks into a layout, with the same design tokens as the rest of the platform so a message cannot look like it came from a different company.
- Lists and segments: Target by tag, pipeline stage, service, area, spend, last visit or any combination, because a segment is a query over real records.
- A unified inbox: Replies arrive in the platform and attach to the account, so a response to a campaign is a conversation on the timeline, not a message in a separate tool.
- Results that mean something: Opens, clicks, replies, unsubscribes, and the harder number: revenue attributed to the campaign against the accounts it touched.

## Deliverability is the whole game

A beautiful campaign that lands in a promotions tab or a spam folder did not happen. Most small business email fails here, not in the writing.

AlphaFlux sends from a domain you control and sets up the authentication records that mailbox providers check before they decide whether to trust a message. Sending from your own domain means your reputation is yours, rather than borrowed from a shared sender that another company can damage for you.

Bounces, complaints and unsubscribes are handled automatically. A customer who opts out is suppressed everywhere, including from messages an agent would send, because consent is a property of the customer rather than a setting on a campaign.

Sending is separated from transactional mail. A receipt or an appointment confirmation is one kind of message, and a marketing offer is another, and mixing them is what turns a useful notification into a spam complaint.

- Authentication handled: The records mailbox providers check are configured and kept correct, so your domain carries its own reputation.
- Consent is respected: An unsubscribe suppresses across every campaign, every sequence and anything an agent sends.
- Bounces acted on: Hard bounces are removed, soft bounces retried, and the reasons are visible rather than counted.
- Separated from notifications: Transactional messages and marketing messages travel on different rails, so a reminder never looks like an advertisement.

## Sequences worth having on day one

These are the automations that pay for the module, and each one is triggered by an event the platform already records.

- Missed call recovery: A call to the business that is not answered triggers a text immediately and an email shortly after, asking whether the customer still needs help. This is usually the highest returning sequence a service business can run.
- Quote follow up: A quote that has not been accepted after a set number of days triggers a short follow up. Most quotes are not lost, they are forgotten, by both sides.
- Before the visit: A confirmation before an appointment, with what to expect and how to prepare. This reduces wasted trips more reliably than any reminder system a customer has to opt into.
- After the visit: A thank you, a receipt, a request for a review, and any paperwork the customer needs to keep. Sent while the work is still memorable.
- Lapsed customer win back: A customer who has not booked in a set period gets a sequence that offers a reason to come back, timed to the season or the service interval rather than to a generic calendar.
- Review request: Ask for a review at the moment satisfaction is highest, which is minutes after a completed visit, and route the response to the platform's own review page.

## Why the inbox belongs inside the platform

Email marketing tools are good at sending and bad at knowing anything. They have their own list, their own idea of who a customer is, and no idea that the person on it is ninety days overdue or just had a complaint resolved yesterday.

Because AlphaFlux sends from records rather than from a copied list, a campaign can exclude customers with an open complaint, segment on a pipeline stage, and count revenue against the accounts it touched. A reply lands on the account timeline next to the job it relates to.

That is what makes the reporting real instead of decorative. A campaign that reports a twenty percent open rate and no attributable revenue has not told anyone anything useful.

### Is the free plan enough to send anything useful?

It is enough to keep in touch with a small customer base and to run a missed call recovery sequence, which is often the one that matters most. A hundred marketing messages a month covers a solo operator with a few dozen regular customers. When the list outgrows it, that is usually a good sign.

### Can I send from my own email address?

Yes, from a domain you control. Sending from your own domain means your reputation is yours and your customers see your name. The platform sets up the authentication records that mailbox providers check and keeps them correct.

### What about customers who unsubscribed?

They are suppressed permanently, across every campaign, every automated sequence and anything an agent sends. The suppression is a property of the customer record, so it cannot be bypassed by starting a new campaign.

### Do receipts and appointment reminders count toward my allowance?

No. Transactional messages such as receipts, confirmations and reminders travel separately and are not counted against the marketing allowance, because they are expected communication rather than marketing.

### Can I see whether a campaign made money?

On the plans that include attribution, yes. Revenue is counted against the accounts a campaign touched, using the jobs and invoices the platform already holds, rather than a tracking pixel's best guess.

# Decide where to grow, then prove it worked

URL: https://alphaflux.net/marketing
Section: Modules

Most marketing tools stop at the message. This one starts a step earlier, with the map and the numbers that tell you which area is worth the drive, and finishes with the revenue the campaign actually produced.

## The growth work, in one place

Finding customers, keeping them, and knowing which channel paid for itself.

- Territory planning: Draw the areas you want to work in, save each one with its own notes and pursuit status, and see at a glance which are prospects and which are earning.
- Demographics on the map: Population, income, age, housing and education for any area you draw, so a decision about coverage is made on data rather than on a drive past.
- Social scheduling: Connect your accounts, write a post once, schedule it, and keep a calendar of what is going out and when.
- Reviews at the right moment: Ask for a review minutes after a completed visit rather than days later, when the customer can still remember the technician's name.
- Attribution to revenue: Which campaign, channel or referral produced the jobs, and what those jobs were worth, out of the same records as the invoices.
- Your public presence: Landing pages and a booking entry point that feed directly into the schedule, with availability answered from real capacity.

## Most marketing decisions should be made on a map

Where a service business grows is a geographic question, and it is usually answered by intuition and a long drive.

Draw an area on the map and the platform returns the demographic picture for it: how many households, what they earn, how old they are, whether they own or rent. Compare two candidate areas side by side and the decision stops being a feeling.

Layer that against where the work already is and the answer gets sharper still. An area adjacent to your densest cluster is cheaper to serve than one across the county, and the platform shows both the opportunity and the drive.

Each saved area carries a pursuit status and its own notes, so a plan that spans a year does not live in one person's head. It lives on a map that anyone with permission can open.

- Areas and zones: Saved service areas, target areas and zones, drawn directly on the map and reused for routing, capacity and pricing.
- Real demographic data: Census and mapping data served through the platform, so no third party script follows your customers around the internet.
- Density and drive time: See where jobs cluster and what adding an area would cost in travel, because revenue per mile is the number that decides whether growth is real.
- A plan with dates: Each area carries where it is in the pursuit, so a quarterly review is a look at the map rather than a reconstruction.

## Everything the module reports on

Attribution only means something if it reaches the money. These are the links the platform already has.

- Lead source and campaign: Every account records where it came from and which campaign touched it, as two separate facts rather than as one field that has to serve both purposes.
- Booked by: Whether a person, an agent or an import created the work, so the value of automation is measurable rather than asserted.
- Revenue by source: Revenue counted from the invoices on accounts a channel produced, over a date range you choose.
- Referrals: Referred accounts record who referred them, so a customer who sends business is visible and can be thanked.
- Cost per acquisition: Enter what a channel costs and the platform reports what it returned, which is the only comparison that settles an argument about marketing spend.

Marketing that cannot be traced to an invoice is a hobby with a budget.

It gives you landing pages and an online booking entry point that are wired to real availability, which is what most service company websites fail at. A company that wants to keep its existing site can keep it and use these for campaigns.

# The conversation and the record, in the same place

URL: https://alphaflux.net/team
Section: Modules

A company does not need another chat app. It needs the conversation about a customer to sit on the customer, where the next person to open the account will actually find it.

## Working together without a second tool

The work is in the field and the decisions are in the office. Both should leave a trail on the account.

- Channels and direct messages: Public channels, private channels, one to one messages and group conversations, with reactions, edits and search.
- A note on the account: Anything worth remembering goes on the customer, not in a private message, so the next person sees it.
- Mentions that notify: Mention a colleague on a note or a message and they are told. Mention an account and it becomes a link.
- Unread that is honest: Unread counts per channel and per conversation, so nothing is missed without a notification firing for every message.
- Search across everything: Find a message, a note, a job or a document by what was said in it, not only by where it lives.
- Shifts and availability: Who is on today, who is off, and who has the right skills, so the schedule is built from reality.

## Roles, departments and what each person can reach

Permissions are explicit per capability rather than implied by a job title, and a role can be scoped to a part of the company.

- Account classes: A platform owner manages the installation, the module catalogue and the companies on it. A user belongs to one company, has a role, and optionally a department.
- Roles: Owner, administrator, office manager, dispatcher, technician, billing, marketing, support and read only auditor. Roles are composable, and a person can hold more than one.
- Departments: A department is a slice of a company: a district, an office, a line of service. A role scoped to a department means a dispatcher in one office cannot see or change another office's work, and the restriction is applied in the query rather than hidden on screen.
- Explicit permissions: View jobs, edit a schedule, collect a payment, export data, manage billing, manage users. Each is a named permission attached to a role and a scope, so access is a decision rather than a side effect.
- Restriction states designed in: A restricted action is refused by the server with the reason named, and the interface shows the disabled state with an explanation rather than failing silently.

## An audit trail, not a log file

Every change records who acted, under what role, for which company, doing what, and when.

The owner sees every entry across the installation. A company user sees their own company's entries. Nothing about that is optional, and nothing bypasses it, including actions taken by an agent or by a scheduled job.

That is what makes a bad afternoon recoverable. When a schedule was changed and the customer is annoyed, the answer is not a guess. It is a filtered list with a name on it.

It is also what makes automation safe to adopt. An owner can see exactly what an agent has been doing, in the same view as what their staff have been doing, and can turn it off with evidence rather than on a hunch.

- Attributed actions: Person, agent or import, recorded on the action itself rather than inferred.
- Overrides flagged: A capacity override, a forced booking or a manual adjustment is recorded with the person who made it.
- Filterable: Filter by person, role, company, action or date range, and read it as a list rather than scrolling a raw file.
- Readable by an agent: The audit log is an endpoint, so an agent can summarise it, spot a pattern, or alert on an unusual change.

## Why the chat polls instead of streaming

Team chat in AlphaFlux updates by asking the server for anything new rather than by holding a constant connection open. That is a deliberate choice, and it is worth explaining because it affects what the product feels like.

A persistent connection per user is a thing to run, secure and monitor, and on a platform where the AI and the database are already competing for a finite machine, that cost buys less than it appears to. Polling with a proper cursor is simple, survives a dropped connection without a state machine, and works behind the corporate networks and field connections that a real service business operates on.

The honest trade is that typing indicators and presence, the little signals that make a chat product feel alive, are not part of it. That is the correct trade for a system whose job is to hold the record straight rather than to be the place people hang out.


If a decision about a customer lives in a private message, it did not get made.


## Team and collaboration by plan


| Users | 1 | 3 | 10 | 25 and above |
| Account timeline and notes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Mentions and notifications | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Team chat | no | yes | yes | yes |

### Do I still need a separate chat app?

For conversations about customers, probably not. AlphaFlux chat keeps the discussion on the account where it belongs. Companies that also want a general purpose chat tool for lunch plans are welcome to keep one, but the customer conversation is better on the customer.

### Can I stop one office seeing another office's customers?

Yes. A role scoped to a department restricts access at the query level, so a dispatcher in one district cannot see, search or change another district's records. It is enforced on the server rather than hidden in the interface.

### Can a technician see pricing?

That is a permission, not a fixed rule. A company can give technicians the job detail without the money, or the money without the customer's payment history, according to how it wants to run.

### What happens to a chat message if someone leaves?

It stays on the record. Messages are attributed to the person, and deactivating an account removes access without deleting the history, because a conversation about a customer is part of that customer's file.

### Does the audit log slow the platform down?

No. Entries are written alongside the change they describe rather than in a separate pass, and the log is designed to be read in filtered slices rather than scanned in full.

---

# The numbers an owner reads, and what to do about them

URL: https://alphaflux.net/analytics
Section: Modules

Most dashboards tell you what happened. This one tells you what happened, where, and what the two or three things worth acting on this week are.

## What the owner's view shows

Every figure comes from the records the work produced. Nothing here is typed in by hand or projected forward.

- Customers and non customers: Real customers counted separately from leads, prospects and empty records, which is the difference between a real number and an inflated one.
- Recurring revenue: Monthly recurring revenue computed from the actual charges on live agreements, per location and combined.
- Work completed: Jobs completed in a period, per technician and per location, with the completed quantity rather than the scheduled quantity.
- Distance travelled: Miles driven, computed from check in and check out positions on completed jobs, which is the number that tells you whether your routes are sane.
- Collected and owed: Revenue collected in the period and the overdue balance with its age, side by side, because a good month that is uncollected is not a good month.
- Trends, not snapshots: Compare a period against the one before it and see which figures moved, rather than reading a single number with no context.

## An advisor that has read your numbers before it speaks

General business advice is free and everywhere. Advice that knows your overdue balance, your technician count and your recurring book is not.

The advisor takes a short brief about the business and then answers using the live figures the platform already holds. It does not guess at your customer count, and it does not offer advice that ignores whether you have the capacity to execute it.

Ask it where to focus this quarter and it will weigh what it knows: how much of your revenue is recurring, how much is sitting overdue, how the work is distributed across technicians, and which areas are producing. The answer comes back with specific priorities rather than a list of categories.

It runs on a model of your choosing, including one running on your own hardware, which is the arrangement that keeps your operating numbers inside your building.

- Grounded in real figures: The live metrics are given to the advisor, so the plan is about your business rather than about business in general.
- Prioritised: A short ordered list of what to do next, not a survey of everything that could be done.
- Aggregates only: The advisor receives summary figures, not customer records. Nothing identifying a customer is put in front of a model.
- Ask it on a schedule: Run it weekly or monthly and have the result delivered, so the review happens without anyone remembering to do it.

## The reports the platform produces

Every one of these reads from the same records, so two reports never disagree with each other.

- Operations: Jobs completed, on time percentage, average time on site, jobs per technician, distance travelled and route utilisation, by location and period.
- Revenue: Collected, invoiced, outstanding and overdue, with the age of the debt, by location, service and period.
- Recurring book: How many agreements are active, what they are worth monthly, what has been added and what has been cancelled, with cancellations reported rather than buried.
- Sales attribution: Revenue by lead source, by campaign and by the person who booked it, with agent generated revenue shown separately so automation can be judged on its results.
- Inventory and usage: Stock position per location, usage per technician, consumption per service, and variance against counts.
- Customer communication: Calls answered and missed, response times, messages sent and received, reviews requested and received.

## Why the honest number is usually the smaller one

Dashboards that are assembled from several systems tend to overstate. A lead record gets counted as a customer. A scheduled job gets counted as work done. A recurring charge gets projected twelve times because it looked like a subscription.

The figures here are deliberately conservative. A customer is a customer because the record says so. A job counts when it is completed and dated. Recurring revenue is what the agreements actually charge, divided by their actual frequency.

That has a consequence worth stating plainly. The first time an owner sees this dashboard, the numbers often look worse than what they were used to. They are not worse. They are the first ones that were real, and every decision made from them is made on ground that holds.


A number that looks good because of how it was counted is not a result. It is a delay.


## Reporting by plan


| Basic dashboard | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Per location splits | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Recurring revenue reporting | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Route and distance reporting | no | no | yes | yes |
| Attribution and commission reports | no | Basic | yes | yes |
| The advisor | no | no | yes | yes |
| Scheduled delivery of reports | no | no | yes | yes |
| Consolidated view across companies | no | no | no | yes |

### Can I export the underlying data rather than just the report?

Yes. Every report has the records behind it available as structured data through the interface and over the API, so a figure can be traced to the rows that produced it rather than taken on trust.

### How is distance calculated for a technician's day?

From the check in and check out positions recorded on completed jobs, which makes it a measurement of what happened rather than a route plan's estimate of what should have happened.

### Can I see figures for one district only?

Yes, on the plans that include location splits. A manager scoped to one district sees that district, and an owner sees every district side by side or combined.

### Does the advisor need internet access?

It needs a model, and that model can be hosted or local. Organisations that keep their operating numbers on their own hardware can run the advisor against a model on the same machine.

### Can I schedule a report to be emailed?

Yes on the plans that include scheduled delivery. A weekly digest can go to the owner, the office manager and anyone else who needs it, without anyone logging in to produce it.

## Every plan shows the same small badge until you white label

That is a deliberate design decision rather than a limitation, and it is worth explaining because it is unusual.

- Why the badge is there: A customer facing page carries a small line stating that the platform is provided by AlphaFlux. It is how a company we host can be discovered, and it is how a free plan costs nothing.
- What it looks like: A single unobtrusive line in the footer of the pages your customers see. It is not on your internal dashboards and it never appears in your emails, your invoices or your branding.
- How to remove it: White label removes it entirely, along with every other trace of AlphaFlux, and gives you the platform under your own name with resale rights.

## Moving up never means migrating

The most common reason a small business avoids software is the fear that starting cheap means starting over later.

Every plan runs the same platform on the same records. Moving from one to the next lifts a limit and unlocks modules. Nothing is exported, nothing is re-imported, and nothing that was entered under a smaller plan is withheld until it is paid for.

Limits are visible before they are reached, so an upgrade is a decision rather than an emergency. And if a limit is hit at an inconvenient moment, the platform stops the next record rather than locking the ones you already have.

A company can also add a single module to any plan without changing plan at all, which is usually how it goes: one thing is currently costing money, so that one thing gets added.

- Same records: No export, no import, no reconciliation. The account you built on Free is the account you have on Scale.
- Limits announced early: Approaching a limit is visible on the dashboard so the decision is never made under pressure.
- Single modules available: Add one module to any plan rather than changing the whole thing.
- Change when you want: Move up, move down or add a module at any time, effective immediately, with no notice period.

A free plan that expires was never a free plan. It was a countdown.


## Programs that take money off

These apply on top of any plan, including the paid ones, and they stack with nothing else.

- Nonprofits and faith organizations: A registered nonprofit, church or faith based organization receives the Growth plan at no cost, verified once and kept for as long as the organization qualifies.
- Military and veterans: Thirty percent off any paid plan, for active service members and veterans, verified once.
- First responders: Thirty percent off any paid plan for firefighters, police officers, emergency medical staff and dispatchers.
- Nurses and healthcare staff: Thirty percent off any paid plan for registered nurses and clinical staff.

### Is the free plan really free forever?

Yes. There is no expiry, no card on file and no automatic conversion to a paid plan. Companies move up when their own workload outgrows those limits, not because a timer ran out.

### What counts as a location?

A base you operate from: a town, an office, a depot or a service area. A company working out of one place is one location. A company with crews in three states needs three, because each one has its own schedule, staff and capacity.

### Why is white label five thousand a month?

Because it is not a plan, it is a platform. Whoever buys it gets every module with no limits, their own branding and domain, email under their own sending identity, their own bundles and pricing, and the right to resell it to their own customers. That is an operator's cost, and it is priced as one.

No. Plans are monthly and can be changed at any time. Annual billing is available and carries a discount for companies that prefer it.

The plan reverts to the free tier rather than the account being closed. If your usage exceeds what the free plan covers, you keep read access to everything and can export it in full. Nothing is held hostage and nothing is deleted on a payment lapse.

### Can I get a discount for a nonprofit?

Yes, registered nonprofits and faith based organizations receive the Growth plan at no cost. Military, veterans, nurses, firefighters, police and emergency medical staff receive thirty percent off any paid plan. Both are verified once and are described in full on the community programs page.

### Is there a setup fee or a contract?

Neither on the standard plans. There is no implementation fee, no onboarding charge and no minimum term. White label and enterprise arrangements are agreed individually because they involve work beyond turning features on.

# Built for anyone whose work happens at somebody else's address

URL: https://alphaflux.net/industries
Section: Company

If a truck, a van or a technician goes somewhere, does the work and needs to prove it happened, this platform fits. The same records serve a one van pest control route and a fleet of mobile units scattered across three states.

## Where it fits, and what the fit looks like

These are not industry templates with different colours. They are the same modules, arranged around the way each business actually runs.

- Pest control: Recurring treatment agreements with a genuine frequency model, service areas and territory rules, chemical usage recorded against the property, technician stock on the truck, and an AI receptionist that can tell an emergency sting call from a routine quote request.
  - Quarterly, monthly and seasonal agreements that generate their own visits
  - Chemical sign in and sign out with per property application records
  - Do not service lists, territory rules and re-service tracking
  - State and federal reporting on applications, available on demand
- Plumbing, HVAC and electrical: Emergency work arriving at unpredictable hours, capacity that is genuinely limited by the number of vans, and invoices that need parts, labour and a signature on them before the van leaves.
  - After hours call handling that routes an emergency to a person immediately
  - Capacity rules that stop a day being oversold by a dispatcher in a hurry
  - Parts drawn from the technician's own stock as the job closes
  - Proof of work captured before the technician drives away
- Roofing, solar and exterior trades: Long jobs, permits and inspections, and the same customer coming back after a storm. Work that has to survive a weather delay without losing its history.
  - Jobs that span days with their own history and status flow
  - Photo evidence at each stage, attached to the job rather than texted to an office phone
  - Storm and weather data on the map for planning and for documentation
  - Maintenance and warranty tracking on installed equipment
- Mobile and self contained units: Operations built around units that move: mobile workshops, solar powered field units, trailers, containers and remote stations deployed wherever the work is. The unit and its contents move together and both need a position and a custodian.
  - A unit tracked as both an asset and a location, with its own stock position
  - Custody of whatever is inside it and who is responsible for it
  - Maintenance schedules and service history by unit
  - A consolidated view across every unit, whichever site it is sitting on
- Cleaning and janitorial: Recurring contracts, multi site accounts, crews rather than individual technicians, and a client who wants proof that the work happened at each site.
  - Multi site accounts with checklists and photo proof per site
  - Crew based scheduling rather than one technician per job
  - Client facing completion reports generated from the work itself
  - Consumable stock tracked across every site and every vehicle
- Security patrol: Rounds that have to be provable, checkpoints that can be scanned, and a client who wants the log rather than a summary of it.
  - Checkpoint scanning from a phone with a location and a time on each scan
  - Rounds logs per site, per officer and per shift
  - Incident reporting that attaches to the site and the shift
  - Client access to the record without a report being assembled by hand
- Landscaping and grounds: Route dense work where the drive between sites is the cost. Density and sequencing are the whole margin.
  - Dense route sequencing across many short stops
  - Seasonal agreements and service intervals
  - Distance and utilisation reporting per crew and per day
  - Equipment and consumable tracking across vehicles
- Logistics, delivery and haulage: Orders rather than jobs, a board rather than a list, and customers who want to watch a vehicle approach.
  - Order board with custom stages per order type
  - Live map of orders, vehicles and drivers with arrival estimates
  - Multi stop manifests for a single run
  - Customer tracking links that show one order and nothing else
- Construction and general contracting: Projects, change orders, subcontractors and a schedule that has to survive a supplier being late. The same customer, many jobs, and money that has to be tracked per job rather than per month.
  - Job costing with line items, change orders and retention
  - Subcontractor and supplier records with their own paperwork
  - Progress photos and sign offs per stage
  - Inventory across sites, yards and lock ups
- Industrial, additive and aerospace: Some of the same problems at a different scale: assets with service lives and certifications, tooling and materials that must be traceable, and documentation that has to survive an audit years later.
  - Asset registers with service intervals, calibration and warranty
  - Material and component traceability through sign in and sign out
  - Work orders and maintenance history on every machine
  - An audit trail on every record change, readable and exportable
- Nonprofits, faith organizations and community groups: Volunteers rather than employees, service users rather than customers, and a budget that has to be spent on the mission. The free organization plan is built for exactly this.
  - A free plan available to any registered nonprofit or faith organization
  - Volunteer scheduling and shift coverage
  - Service logs, check ins and follow ups on the people served
  - Grant and programme reporting from the records the work produced

## Why one platform fits all of these

The industries look different from the outside and are almost identical from the inside. Somebody needs something done at a place, by a person, on a date, for a price, and then needs to prove it and get paid.

That is the same record in every case. A pest control visit, a plumbing call out, a delivery, a patrol round and a cleaning job are all a customer, a place, a person, a time, a price, an outcome and a proof. Once that is one object, the industry differences become configuration rather than different software.

Which is why the same platform can run a two person operation on the free plan and a fleet of mobile units with several hundred sites. What changes is the number of locations, the modules switched on, and the stages the work passes through, all of which are settings.

It also means a company that grows into a different line of work does not have to buy a second system. The second line of business is another module and another order type, sharing the same customers.

- Order types: Define your own job or order types with their own stages, required fields and proof rules.
- One customer, many services: A customer who buys recurring treatment and a one off repair is one account with two kinds of work.
- Inventory that fits the trade: Consumables for cleaning, chemicals and regulated stock for pest control, parts and materials for trade work, tools and tooling everywhere.
- Billing that matches the trade: Recurring agreements for contract work, job costing for projects, per stop pricing for route work, all in the same ledger.

The industry is not the differentiator. Whether the truck was where it said it was is.


## What every one of them gets

- Free inventory, always: Stock and custody on every plan including the free one, because a one van operation needs to know what is in the van as much as a depot does.
- A phone that answers: Missed call text back on every plan, and an AI receptionist that books real work once the business is big enough to need one.
- Agents that can act: Scoped access so software can book, chase, report and update records without a password being shared.
- A record that holds up: Every change attributed, every financial record preserved, every proof attached to the job it belongs to.

### Do you have a template for my industry?

There are starting configurations for the common trades that set sensible order types, stages and required fields, so a new account does not begin with a blank slate. Beyond that, the configuration is yours to change.

### My business does not fit any of these.

Then test it against the underlying shape: does somebody need something done at a place, by a person, on a date, for a price, and then need to prove it and get paid. If that describes the work, the platform fits, whatever the trade is called.

### Can I run two different businesses on one account?

Yes, as two companies under one operator, each with its own records and its own modules, or as one company with two order types. Which is better depends on whether the two businesses share customers and money.

### Does it work outside the United States?

Addressing, currency, time zone and phone handling are configurable per company, so it works in other English speaking markets and in any market where the carrier side is available.

### Is there an industry the platform genuinely does not suit?

Businesses where the work has no location and no scheduled appointment, such as pure software or retail over a counter. Those are better served by something else, and it is better to say so than to sell around it.

# Some of the people who need this most are not trying to make a lot of money

URL: https://alphaflux.net/programs
Section: Company

A church running a food pantry, a volunteer fire department, a nurse picking up weekend work, a veteran starting a one van operation. The platform can afford to help, so it does.

## The programs

There are two of them. One gives the platform away, and one takes thirty percent off. Both are verified once and then left alone.

- Registered nonprofits: Any registered charitable organization receives the Growth plan at no cost: unlimited customers, locations and users within the plan, every module except the enterprise tier, and no expiry.
- Faith organizations: Churches, synagogues, temples, mosques and any other registered faith organization receive the same free plan on the same terms, because the program is about the work an organization does rather than about what it believes.
- Military and veterans: Thirty percent off any paid plan, for active service members, reservists, national guard and veterans, including the family member running the business.
- Firefighters: Thirty percent off any paid plan, career and volunteer, including wildland crews and the side businesses they run.
- Police and emergency medical: Thirty percent off any paid plan for sworn officers, dispatchers, emergency medical technicians and paramedics.
- Nurses and clinical staff: Thirty percent off any paid plan for registered nurses, licensed practical nurses and clinical staff, including the home care and mobile services many of them run.

## Why the faith program is not limited to one faith

It is worth stating the policy plainly rather than leaving it to be inferred, because a policy that excludes some houses of worship and not others is not one a business should have.

The free plan is offered to registered faith organizations on identical terms regardless of which faith they practise. A church, a synagogue, a temple and a mosque running the same kind of community work get the same account, the same modules and the same support.

There are two reasons, and the second one matters more than the first. The first is legal: a commercial service that gives away an account to one religion and refuses another is discriminating on the basis of religion, and that is not a defensible position for a business to hold in writing.

The second is that the program exists because community organizations do work that is worth helping, and the food pantry, the shelter, the burial fund and the after school program are not the property of any one congregation. Helping the work means helping whoever is doing it.

- Same terms, same support: Identical plan, identical limits and identical support for every registered faith organization.
- No creed test: Verification is about the organization's registration and the work it does, not about its doctrine.
- The intention is unchanged: The purpose is to put a capable system in the hands of organizations that spend their money on people rather than on software.

## What each program actually includes

Not a coupon code and not a discount on a first month. A real account with real capability.

- The nonprofit and faith account: The Growth plan at no cost. That is unlimited customers and locations within the plan, ten users, ten thousand marketing emails a month, five phone numbers, the AI receptionist, the dispatch board, email marketing from their own domain, the advisor and the full reporting.
  - No card, no expiry and no automatic conversion to a paid plan
  - The same support as a paying customer on the same plan
  - If the organization grows past the Growth limits, the next plan has the discount already applied
- The thirty percent service discount: Thirty percent off any paid plan, applied to the monthly price, for as long as the person is eligible. It combines with nothing else and it does not expire while the eligibility holds.
  - Applies to Starter, Growth, Scale and Enterprise
  - Applies to the business the person owns or operates, not only to a personal account
  - Can be applied after signing up, with the difference credited forward

## How verification works

- Apply: Request the program from inside the account after signing up on the free plan. No forms by email and no waiting on a sales call.
- Prove it once: A registration number for an organization, or a document for an individual: a veteran's identification, a certification, a department identification or an employer letter.
- It applies: The discount or the plan change is applied to the account, and nothing further is asked for. It is not re-verified every year unless the eligibility itself is time limited.

A verification that is done once and then forgotten is the difference between a program and a form.


## Why this is affordable to offer

A free account costs the platform very little. The infrastructure is shared, the modules already exist, and an organization using the platform is likely to be one that tells other organizations about it. The economics work because the software is built and the marginal cost of one more company on it is close to nothing.

It is also the right shape for a platform that was built by someone running a service business rather than by a venture funded team optimising for a metric. The point of the product is that a small operator can afford what a large one has. That argument is weaker if small operators are the only people who never get a break.

So the programs are permanent rather than promotional, and they are stated with their limits on the page rather than negotiated in a call.


### Is the free nonprofit account really free, permanently?

Yes. No card, no expiry, no automatic conversion to a paid plan. If the organization later grows past the Growth plan's limits, the next plan up has the relevant discount applied rather than starting from full price.

### Which faith organizations qualify?

Any registered faith organization, of any faith, on identical terms. Verification looks at the organization's registration and the work it does rather than at its beliefs.

### I am a veteran running a company. Does the discount apply to the business?

Yes. The discount applies to the business the person owns or operates, not only to a personal account. It is thirty percent off any paid plan.

### Can I combine a discount with anything else?

Discounts do not stack with each other, and the free organization plan is not discounted further because it already costs nothing. One program per account.

### How long does verification take?

Usually the same day. The check is against a registration number or a document, not against a decision by a committee.

### What documents do you accept for the service discount?

A veteran's identification or a discharge document, a department or station identification, a professional certification or licence number, or an employer letter. Anything that establishes the eligibility is acceptable, and the review is done by a person rather than an automated check.

# Every capability is an interface first, and a screen second

URL: https://alphaflux.net/developers
Section: Company

There is nothing you can do in the console that you cannot do over the API. That is a design rule rather than an aspiration, and it is what allows an agent to run real work here instead of describing it.

## The four ways in

Pick the one that fits, or use all of them. They reach the same records under the same permissions.

- The REST API: Every module exposes its operations over HTTP with JSON in and JSON out. A machine readable specification is published, so a client can be generated rather than hand written, and an agent can discover the available operations without being told about them.
  - Bearer authentication with scoped keys
  - A published specification describing every operation and its rules
  - Consistent conventions for filtering, pagination and errors
  - Credentials are never returned, including in responses that would otherwise echo them
- The command line: One binary that talks to the same API and prints JSON, which means it pipes into another tool or straight into a script. It includes generic call and post commands, so a new endpoint is usable before a typed wrapper exists.
  - Around forty commands covering the whole platform
  - Every command outputs JSON
  - A generic call and post for anything not yet wrapped
  - Configured with two environment variables
- The agent protocol server: A server that presents the platform to an agent client as a set of callable tools over a standard protocol. It runs as a local process the client launches, holds no state of its own, and authenticates with the same scoped key.
  - Point any compatible agent client at it with two settings
  - Each tool maps to an API operation with typed arguments and a description
  - Permissions come from the key, so the tool list is the permission list
- Webhooks and callbacks: The platform receives events from carriers and providers, verifies them, and acts on them. Outbound notification for your own integrations follows the same model, so an external system can be told when work changes rather than polling for it.

## A request, and what comes back

Authenticate with a scoped key and ask for identity. Everything else follows the same shape.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ALPHAFLUX_API_KEY" \
  https://alphaflux.net/api/me

{
  "email": "you@example.com",
  "roles": ["owner"],
  "tenants": [
    {
      "name": "Northside Services",
      "role": "owner",
      "plan": "growth",
      "modules": ["phone", "field", "crm", "inventory", "billing", "email"]
    }
  ]
}


## The same thing from the command line

JSON out, so it composes. The last two commands reach any endpoint, including ones that do not have a typed command yet.

export ALPHAFLUX_API_KEY=afx_...
export ALPHAFLUX_BASE=https://alphaflux.net

alphaflux me
alphaflux field jobs add --customer "Acme LLC" --service "Treatment" --date 2026-10-02
alphaflux field status --id fs_job:abc123 --status done
alphaflux phone text --to +15095551234 --body "On the way"
alphaflux billing run
alphaflux key create --label dispatch-agent --scopes "field:write,phone:read"

alphaflux call api/dashboard
alphaflux post api/notes --json '{"account":"fieldroutes:10000","body":"Called back, no answer"}'


## How keys and scopes work

An integration is a credential with a job to do. Nothing about the design assumes a human holds it.

- Scoped read and write: Access is granted per module, so an integration that books work does not need the billing module and does not get it.
- Hashed and shown once: A key is displayed at the moment it is created and stored only as a hash. Losing one means issuing a new one, not recovering the old one.
- Inherits its owner: A key carries exactly the permissions and companies of the account that created it, and cannot reach past them.
- Revocable immediately: Disable a key and every request using it stops. Nothing else on the account is disturbed.
- Optional expiry: A key can be issued with an expiry date for temporary or contractor access.
- Every use is recorded: Actions are written to the audit trail against the account that owns the key, so a key is never anonymous.

## Why the platform was built this way

Most business software treats its API as a concession. It exists, it lags the interface, and some things are simply not exposed. That is no longer a defensible position now that a meaningful share of work is done by software talking to software.

The rule here is the opposite. A capability is designed as an interface first and then wrapped in a screen. The screen is a client. The command line is a client. An agent is a client. If something is missing from one of them, it is a bug rather than a decision.

It also future proofs the work. When an operation is available over a documented interface with a machine readable specification, the next tool that needs it does not require anyone's permission or a new integration project. It reads the specification and does the work.

And it means the audit trail is complete. An agent, a script, a scheduled job and a person all arrive through the same door, so every change is attributable to something identifiable rather than to root.


## What each plan includes


| Console access | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| REST API | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Published API specification | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Command line | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Agent protocol server | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Scoped API keys | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Webhooks | no | no | yes | yes |
| Your own API surface for your customers | no | no | no | yes |

### Is there a sandbox?

Yes. A test company can be created alongside the real one with its own records and its own keys, so an integration can be built and broken without touching live data.

### Are there rate limits?

Requests are rate limited per key to protect the platform, and the limit is generous enough that a normal integration never meets it. The response headers tell you where you are against the limit rather than leaving you to discover it by being refused.

### What happens if an integration breaks something?

Everything it did is attributed to its key and visible in the audit trail, and the key can be disabled immediately. Financial records are voided rather than deleted and merges are reversible, so a bad batch can be walked back.

### Can I use an agent client that is not yours?

Yes. The agent server speaks a standard protocol, so any compatible client can use it. There is nothing proprietary about the connection, and the key is the only thing that decides what the agent can reach.

### Can I build my own product on top of this?

That is what white label is for. It gives you the platform under your own brand with resale rights, and the same interfaces to build against.

# Every page on this site

URL: https://alphaflux.net/sitemap
Section: Company

Grouped the same way the navigation rail groups them, so the map and the interface agree.

## The whole site

If you are looking for something specific, it is on this page.


## For machines

This site is built to be read by software as well as by people. These are the files published for that purpose.

- sitemap.xml (https://alphaflux.net/sitemap.xml): The standard sitemap, listing every page with its last modified date and a priority. Linked from robots.txt.
- robots.txt (https://alphaflux.net/robots.txt): Crawl rules. Everything on this site is public product documentation, and answer engines and AI crawlers are explicitly welcome across all of it rather than tolerated.
- llms.txt (https://alphaflux.net/llms.txt): A short index written for language models: what the platform is, what each module does, the pricing structure and how the discount programs work.
- llms-full.txt (https://alphaflux.net/llms-full.txt): The full text of every page in one file, so an answer engine can read the whole site without fetching each page separately.
- Structured data (application/ld+json on every page): Every page publishes structured data describing the organisation, the breadcrumb trail, and where relevant the product, the plans and the questions answered on the page. The markup and the visible content match, because structured data describing something the page does not say is a lie told to a machine.
- The API specification (https://alphaflux.net/api/openapi.json): A machine readable description of the platform's own interface, for developers and for agents. Issued with an API key.

### Why publish a file just for language models?

Because a growing share of people find software by asking a question rather than by searching. A file that states plainly what the platform does, what it costs and what the limits are gives an answer engine something accurate to read. Publishing it is a way of being described correctly rather than being guessed at.

### Can I crawl this site?

Yes. Everything here is public product documentation, the crawl rules permit the whole site, and no part of it requires JavaScript to read. Structured data is published on every page describing the same content a person sees.
